headline: High: shared-file and broad-egress defaults make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible; compliance risk is lower but non-zero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress is a chatbot agent and LangGraph can wire developer-defined tools and application-defined files, so a shared workspace or file bridge could let Botpress content influence LangGraph prompts. The pair lacks a documented isolation boundary, but no direct shared channel is shown, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF Botpress outputs are copied into LangGraph file inputs or node prompts
IF the orchestrator exposes a shared filesystem or message queue between the agents
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct workspaces
Disable automatic ingestion of Botpress-generated text into LangGraph prompts
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages
Review any file-based handoff before execution
requires-engineering: add a sanitizer/allowlist for prompt-bearing fields

B_data_leakage.rationale: Botpress has no network egress, but LangGraph has broad egress and handles model provider API keys, so any shared workspace or copied context could leak sensitive content from Botpress into external APIs. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so this is not high, but the default LangGraph egress makes leakage plausible.
conditions: IF Botpress outputs contain secrets or customer data
IF LangGraph nodes forward shared state to model providers or developer-defined tools
mitigations: Keep sensitive Botpress outputs out of shared graph state
Redact secrets before passing data to LangGraph
Restrict LangGraph tools to local-only endpoints
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, while LangGraph can execute shells, spawn subprocesses, read and write application-defined files, and persist shared state across instances. If both operate on the same mutable workspace, concurrent writes and state corruption are plausible by default, with potentially irreversible workflow damage.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory, repo, or checkpointer store
IF LangGraph nodes mutate files while Botpress installs or updates packages
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Lock shared files before writes
Disable package installation in Botpress for shared projects
Run LangGraph with a dedicated checkpointer namespace
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support agent and LangGraph is a stateful orchestration layer that can act on developer-defined tools, so Botpress outputs can become LangGraph inputs and then trigger downstream actions. Without a documented verification step, mistaken Botpress facts can cascade into irreversible or externally visible actions.
conditions: IF LangGraph consumes Botpress responses as authoritative state
IF downstream nodes send emails, update records, or call external APIs based on those responses
mitigations: Insert a human review step before external actions
Require schema validation on Botpress outputs
Add confidence thresholds before tool execution
Log and diff all state transitions
requires-engineering: implement verification nodes for critical facts

E_compliance.rationale: Botpress is open-source with no stated residency or retention controls, while LangGraph explicitly handles model-provider API keys and application-defined graph state. The pair therefore has a plausible compliance gap around retention and data handling, but the profiles do not show a specific regulated data class or residency mismatch, so medium fits.
conditions: IF regulated or customer data is stored in LangGraph graph state
IF Botpress transcripts are retained or forwarded without a documented policy
mitigations: Document retention for both agents
Exclude regulated data from shared state
Confirm vendor DPAs and residency settings
Minimize logging of prompts and outputs
requires-engineering: implement deletion/export workflows
